_about: High-level Ontario health-and-safety and WSIB obligations that BROADLY apply to construction employers/constructors. These are stated at a general, defensible level to support planning and a compliance conversation. They are NOT legal advice and NOT a complete list. Every item must be verified against the current Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA), O. Reg. 213/91 (Construction Projects), related regulations, and WSIB. No specific numeric thresholds, clause numbers, dollar penalties, or WSIB rate/group numbers are asserted here; where a specific value is needed to act, a VERIFY note points to the source.
_disclaimer: Organizational aid only. Confirm applicability to your specific project, roles (constructor/employer/supervisor/worker), and workplace before relying on any item.

internal_responsibility.label: General duties (Internal Responsibility System)
internal_responsibility.summary: OHSA places general duties on employers, supervisors, and workers to take every precaution reasonable in the circumstances to protect workers. Everyone shares responsibility for safety.
internal_responsibility.verify: VERIFY: the specific duties assigned to each role - OHSA (general duties of constructors, employers, supervisors, workers).

worker_orientation_training.label: Worker awareness training and site orientation
worker_orientation_training.summary: Workers and supervisors must receive basic occupational health and safety awareness training, and workers should receive site-specific orientation and task-specific training/instruction before doing hazardous work.
worker_orientation_training.verify: VERIFY: mandatory basic OHS awareness training content and any specific training records required - OHSA / O. Reg. 297/13 (awareness training) / employer policy.

working_at_heights_training.label: Working at Heights (WAH) training
working_at_heights_training.summary: Workers on a construction project who use certain fall-protection methods must complete approved Working at Heights training before that work. Refresher training is required periodically.
working_at_heights_training.verify: VERIFY: which fall-protection work triggers WAH training, the approved training program, and the refresher interval - Ontario (Ministry of Labour) / O. Reg. 213/91 (do NOT assume the refresher period).

fall_protection.label: Fall protection for work at heights
fall_protection.summary: Fall protection is required for work at heights on construction projects. Guardrails are the preferred control; where not practicable, travel restraint or a fall-arrest system with adequate anchorage is used.
fall_protection.verify: VERIFY: the height that triggers fall protection, permitted methods, anchor strength, and clearance/free-fall limits - O. Reg. 213/91 (do NOT assume a number).

ppe.label: Personal protective equipment (PPE)
ppe.summary: Workers must wear required PPE for the hazards present - commonly head protection (hard hat), safety footwear, eye protection, high-visibility apparel, and hearing/respiratory protection where applicable. The employer must ensure PPE is provided/used and maintained.
ppe.verify: VERIFY: which PPE is mandatory for each task and the applicable performance standards/specifications - O. Reg. 213/91 / OHSA.

first_aid.label: First aid
first_aid.summary: Workplaces covered by WSIB must have first-aid equipment, facilities, and trained first-aider(s) appropriate to the number of workers, and must post required first-aid information.
first_aid.verify: VERIFY: required first-aid box contents, number of trained first-aiders, and posting requirements by workplace size - WSIB First Aid Requirements (Reg. 1101) (do NOT assume the numbers).

site_notices_postings.label: Required site notices and postings
site_notices_postings.summary: Certain documents must be posted or kept available at the project - commonly a copy of OHSA and regulations, the health-and-safety policy (where required), first-aid information, emergency/contact information, and (where required) the Notice of Project.
site_notices_postings.verify: VERIFY: the complete list of documents that must be posted/available on a construction project and where - OHSA / O. Reg. 213/91.

notice_of_project.label: Notice of Project (NoP)
notice_of_project.summary: For certain construction projects, the constructor/employer must submit a Notice of Project to the Ministry before work begins.
notice_of_project.verify: VERIFY: the thresholds/criteria that require a Notice of Project and how/when to file it - O. Reg. 213/91 / Ontario Ministry (do NOT assume the dollar or worker thresholds).

jhsc_representative.label: Joint Health and Safety Committee / Health and Safety Representative
jhsc_representative.summary: Depending on the number of workers regularly employed, a workplace may require a Health and Safety Representative or a Joint Health and Safety Committee (JHSC) with certified members.
jhsc_representative.verify: VERIFY: the worker-count thresholds for a Health and Safety Representative vs. a JHSC, and certification requirements - OHSA (do NOT assume the numbers).

whmis_hazardous_materials.label: WHMIS / hazardous materials communication
whmis_hazardous_materials.summary: Where hazardous products are present, the employer must provide WHMIS training, labels, and access to Safety Data Sheets (SDS).
whmis_hazardous_materials.verify: VERIFY: WHMIS training, labelling, and SDS obligations - OHSA / WHMIS regulation (O. Reg. 860 / Reg. 833 exposure limits as applicable).

designated_substances.label: Designated substances and asbestos
designated_substances.summary: Before certain projects (especially demolition/renovation of existing structures), an assessment for designated substances (including asbestos, silica, lead) may be required, and controls/abatement procedures must be followed where present.
designated_substances.verify: VERIFY: when a designated-substances report/assessment is required and the controls for each substance - O. Reg. 490/09 (Designated Substances) / O. Reg. 278/05 (Asbestos).

incident_reporting.label: Injury / incident / fatality reporting
incident_reporting.summary: Certain workplace injuries, critical injuries, occupational illnesses, and fatalities must be reported to the Ministry and/or the JHSC/representative within required timeframes, and records kept. Serious incident scenes may need to be preserved.
incident_reporting.verify: VERIFY: what qualifies as a 'critical injury', to whom and how fast each type of event must be reported, and record-keeping - OHSA / O. Reg. 213/91 (do NOT assume the timeframes).

wsib_coverage.label: WSIB coverage and registration
wsib_coverage.summary: Most construction employers in Ontario must register with WSIB and carry coverage. There are specific rules for construction, including mandatory coverage that can extend to independent operators/sole proprietors in construction.
wsib_coverage.verify: VERIFY: who must register, the mandatory-coverage-in-construction rules and any exemptions, and registration deadlines - WSIB (do NOT assume exemption criteria).

wsib_premiums_reporting.label: WSIB premium reporting and payment
wsib_premiums_reporting.summary: Registered employers must report insurable earnings and pay premiums on schedule, and classify their business activity correctly.
wsib_premiums_reporting.verify: VERIFY: reporting frequency, deadlines, premium rate, and classification for your activity - WSIB (do NOT assume the rate, rate group, or classification code).

wsib_injury_claims.label: WSIB injury reporting / claims and return-to-work
wsib_injury_claims.summary: When a worker is injured or becomes ill from work, the employer generally must report to WSIB within a required timeframe and cooperate in the worker's return to work.
wsib_injury_claims.verify: VERIFY: the deadline to report a work-related injury/illness to WSIB and return-to-work obligations - WSIB (do NOT assume the reporting deadline).

clearance_certificates.label: WSIB clearance certificates (contractor/subcontractor)
clearance_certificates.summary: In construction, businesses commonly must obtain and provide WSIB clearance certificates confirming their account is in good standing before engaging or being paid by another business.
clearance_certificates.verify: VERIFY: when a clearance certificate is required and how it must be obtained/validated - WSIB.

violence_harassment.label: Workplace violence and harassment
violence_harassment.summary: Employers must have workplace violence and harassment policies and programs, assess risks of violence, and investigate incidents/complaints.
violence_harassment.verify: VERIFY: policy, program, risk-assessment, and investigation requirements - OHSA (workplace violence and harassment provisions).
